ctx.x: It was some band; there was Bernie Privin, the guy I used to work with in the old Artie Shaw and Charlie Barnet days, and he had been in the studios for years; he's a wonderful trumpet player in the Louis Armstrong vein. Dick

Hyman was on piano with us and Major Holley on base; Ed Hubbie on trombone, Kenny Davern -- he played both the clarinet and primarily the soprano saxophone -- I have a mental block with that word 'soprano'.

However, on with the story. Kenny played that instrument just about as great as anybody alive today, that I know of. And I mentioned before that we had a little trio with Dick Wellstood, but that's beside the point. Johnny Mince played the clarinet -- Johnny had been in that Tommy Dorsey band in '39, too. It's funny that we all reunite after the years and after the many years in between to pursue our pursuits of music.
